verses.zh: 灵将我举起，带到耶和华殿向东的东门。谁知，在门口有二十五个人，我见其中有民间的首领押朔的儿子雅撒尼亚和比拿雅的儿子毗拉提。
verses.en: A wind[NOTE:1] lifted me up and brought me to the east gate of the Lord’s temple that faces the east. There, at the entrance of the gate, I noticed 25 men. Among them I saw Jaazaniah son of Azzur and Pelatiah son of Benaiah, officials of the people.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “spirit.” See note on “wind” in 2:2.
The phrase officials of the people occurs in Neh 11:1; 1 Chr 21:2; 2 Chr 24:23.

verses.zh: 耶和华对我说：「人子啊，这就是图谋罪孽的人，在这城中给人设恶谋。
verses.en: The Lord[NOTE:1] said to me, “Son of man, these are the men who plot evil and give wicked advice in this city.
notes: Heb “and he”; the referent (the Lord) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 他们说：『盖房屋的时候尚未临近；这城是锅，我们是肉。』
verses.en: They say,[NOTE:1] ‘The time is not near to build houses;[NOTE:2] the city[NOTE:3] is a cooking pot,[NOTE:4] and we are the meat in it.’
notes: The Hebrew verb may mean “think” in this context. This content of what they say (or think) represents their point of view.
The expression build houses may mean “establish families” (Deut 25:9; Ruth 4:11; Prov 24:27).
Heb “she” or “it”; the feminine pronoun refers here to Jerusalem.
Jerusalem is also compared to a pot in Ezek 24:3-8. The siege of the city is pictured as heating up the pot.

verses.zh: 人子啊，因此你当说预言，说预言攻击他们。」
verses.en: Therefore, prophesy against them! Prophesy, son of man!”

verses.zh: 耶和华的灵降在我身上，对我说：「你当说，耶和华如此说：以色列家啊，你们口中所说的，心里所想的，我都知道。
verses.en: Then the Spirit of the Lord came[NOTE:1] upon me and said to me, “Say: ‘This is what the Lord says: This is what you are thinking,[NOTE:2] O house of Israel; I know what goes through your minds.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “fell.”
The Hebrew verb commonly means “to say” but may also mean “to think” (see also v. 3).
Heb “I know the steps of your spirits.”

verses.zh: 你们在这城中杀人增多，使被杀的人充满街道。
verses.en: You have killed many people in this city; you have filled its streets with corpses.’

verses.zh: 所以主耶和华如此说：你们杀在城中的人就是肉，这城就是锅；你们却要从其中被带出去。
verses.en: Therefore, this is what the Sovereign Lord says: ‘The corpses you have dumped[NOTE:1] in the midst of the city[NOTE:2] are the meat, and this city[NOTE:3] is the cooking pot, but I will take you out of it.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “placed.”
Heb “in its midst.”
Heb “she/it.” See v. 3.
Many of the versions have “I will bring you out” (active) rather than “he brought out” (the reading of MT).

verses.zh: 你们怕刀剑，我必使刀剑临到你们。这是主耶和华说的。
verses.en: You fear the sword, so the sword I will bring against you,’ declares the Sovereign Lord.

verses.zh: 我必从这城中带出你们去，交在外邦人的手中，且要在你们中间施行审判。
verses.en: ‘But I will take you out of the city.[NOTE:1] And I will hand you over to foreigners. I will execute judgments on you.
notes: Heb “its midst.”

verses.zh: 你们必倒在刀下；我必在以色列的境界审判你们，你们就知道我是耶和华。
verses.en: You will die by the sword; I will judge you at the border of Israel. Then you will know that I am the Lord.

verses.zh: 这城必不作你们的锅，你们也不作其中的肉。我必在以色列的境界审判你们，
verses.en: This city will not be a cooking pot for you, and you will not[NOTE:1] be meat within it; I will judge you at the border of Israel.
notes: The Hebrew text does not have the negative particle, but it is implied. The negative particle in the previous line does double duty here.

verses.zh: 你们就知道我是耶和华；因为你们没有遵行我的律例，也没有顺从我的典章，却随从你们四围列国的恶规。」
verses.en: Then you will know that I am the Lord, whose statutes you have not followed and whose regulations you have not carried out. Instead you have behaved according to the regulations of the nations around you!’”

verses.zh: 我正说预言的时候，比拿雅的儿子毗拉提死了。于是我俯伏在地，大声呼叫说：「哎！主耶和华啊，你要将以色列剩下的人灭绝净尽吗？」
verses.en: Now, while I was prophesying, Pelatiah son of Benaiah died. Then I threw myself face down and cried out with a loud voice, “Alas, Sovereign Lord! You are completely wiping out the remnant of Israel!”[NOTE:1]
notes: The LXX reads this statement as a question. Compare this to the question in 9:8. It is possible that the interrogative particle has been omitted by haplography. However, an exclamatory statement as in the MT also makes sense, and the LXX may have simply tried to harmonize this passage with 9:8.

verses.zh: 耶和华的话临到我说：
verses.en: Then the Lord’s message came to me:

verses.zh: 「人子啊，耶路撒冷的居民对你的弟兄、你的本族、你的亲属、以色列全家，就是对大众说：『你们远离耶和华吧！这地是赐给我们为业的。』
verses.en: “Son of man, your brothers,[NOTE:1] your relatives,[NOTE:2] and the whole house of Israel, all of them are those to whom the inhabitants of Jerusalem[NOTE:3] have said, ‘They have gone far away[NOTE:4] from the Lord; to us this land has been given as a possession.’
notes: The MT reads “your brothers, your brothers” either for emphasis (D. I. Block, Ezekiel [NICOT], 1:341, n. 1; 346) or as a result of dittography.

The MT reads גְאֻלָּתֶךָ (geʾullatekha, “your redemption-men”), referring to the relatives responsible for deliverance in times of hardship (see Lev 25:25-55). The LXX and Syriac read “your fellow exiles,” assuming an underlying Hebrew text of גָלוּתֶךָ (galutekha) or having read the א (alef) as an internal mater lectionis for holem.
For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
The MT has an imperative form (“go far!”), but it may be read with different vowels as a perfect verb (“they have gone far”).

verses.zh: 所以你当说：『耶和华如此说：我虽将以色列全家远远迁移到列国中，将他们分散在列邦内，我还要在他们所到的列邦，暂作他们的圣所。』
verses.en: “Therefore say: ‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says: Although I have removed them far away among the nations and have dispersed them among the countries, I have been a little[NOTE:1] sanctuary for them among the lands where they have gone.’
notes: Or “have been partially a sanctuary”; others take this as temporal (cf. NASB, NIV, NRSV “a little while”).

verses.zh: 你当说：『主耶和华如此说：我必从万民中招聚你们，从分散的列国内聚集你们，又要将以色列地赐给你们。』
verses.en: “Therefore say: ‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says: When I regather you from the peoples and assemble you from the lands where you have been dispersed, I will give you back the country of Israel.’

verses.zh: 他们必到那里，也必从其中除掉一切可憎可厌的物。
verses.en: “When they return to it, they will remove from it all its detestable things and all its abominations.

verses.zh: 我要使他们有合一的心，也要将新灵放在他们里面，又从他们肉体中除掉石心，赐给他们肉心，
verses.en: I will give them one heart and I will put a new spirit within them;[NOTE:1] I will remove the hearts of stone from their bodies[NOTE:2] and I will give them tender hearts,[NOTE:3]
notes: The MT reads “you”; many Hebrew mss along with the LXX and other ancient versions read “within them.”
Heb “their flesh.”
Heb “heart of flesh.”

verses.zh: 使他们顺从我的律例，谨守遵行我的典章。他们要作我的子民，我要作他们的　神。
verses.en: so that they may follow my statutes and observe my regulations and carry them out. Then they will be my people, and I will be their God.[NOTE:1]
notes: The expression They will be my people, and I will be their God occurs as a promise to Abraham (Gen 17:8), Moses (Exod 6:7), and the nation (Exod 29:45).

verses.zh: 至于那些心中随从可憎可厌之物的，我必照他们所行的报应在他们头上。这是主耶和华说的。」
verses.en: But those whose hearts are devoted to detestable things and abominations, I hereby repay them for what they have done,[NOTE:1] says the Sovereign Lord.”
notes: Heb “their way on their head I have placed.”

verses.zh: 于是，基路伯展开翅膀，轮子都在他们旁边；在他们以上有以色列　神的荣耀。
verses.en: Then the cherubim spread[NOTE:1] their wings with their wheels alongside them while the glory of the God of Israel hovered above them.
notes: Heb “lifted.”

verses.zh: 耶和华的荣耀从城中上升，停在城东的那座山上。
verses.en: The glory of the Lord rose up from within the city and stopped[NOTE:1] over the mountain east of it.
notes: Heb “stood.”

verses.zh: 灵将我举起，在异象中藉着　神的灵将我带进迦勒底地，到被掳的人那里；我所见的异象就离我上升去了。
verses.en: Then a wind[NOTE:1] lifted me up and carried me to the exiles in Babylonia,[NOTE:2] in the vision given to me by the Spirit of God. Then the vision I had seen went up from me.
notes: Or “spirit.” See note on “wind” in 2:2.
Heb “to Chaldea.”

verses.zh: 我便将耶和华所指示我的一切事都说给被掳的人听。
verses.en: So I told the exiles everything[NOTE:1] the Lord had shown me.
notes: Heb “all the words of.”

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible.
Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing
is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: EZEKIEL 11:1-4

1Moreover, the Spirit lifted me up and brought me to the east gate of the Lord's
house which faced eastward. And behold, there were twenty-five men at the entrance of the gate, and among them I saw Jaazaniah son of Azzur and Pelatiah
son of Benaiah, leaders of the people. 2He said to me, "Son of man, these are the men who devise iniquity and give evil advice in this city, 3who
say, 'Is not the time near to build houses? This city is the pot and we are the flesh.' 4Therefore, prophesy against them, son of man, prophesy!"

11:1 "the Spirit lifted me up" This was not the first or last time Ezekiel was impacted by "Spirit" (i.e. no DEFINITE
ARTICLE, cf. Ezek. 2:2; 3:12,14; 8:3; 11:24; 43:5). See full note at Ezek. 3:12.

SPECIAL TOPIC: BREATH, WIND, SPIRIT

SPECIAL TOPIC: SPIRIT IN THE BIBLE

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PERSONHOOD OF THE SPIRIT

SPECIAL TOPIC: TRINITY, II. C.

▣ "the east gate of the Lord's house" We know from Jer. 26:10 that this was a place of
public assembly (like the city gate in local settings). This gate is mentioned in Ezek. 10:19. This is where the portable Throne Chariot lifted up and left the temple area.

▣ "Jaazaniah son of Azzur" There are three others mentioned by this same first name (BDB 24) but who have different
fathers (cf. Ezek. 8:11; 2 Kgs. 25:23; Jer. 35:3). Be careful of confusion.

▣ "Pelatiah" We know nothing of this man (BDB 812). It is obvious that these two men were leaders of the people.
The nobility had been exiled with Ezekiel in 597 B.C. and, therefore, these were new leaders.

NASB, NJB, JPSOA, LXX
"leaders of the people"

NKJV, Peshitta
"princes of the people"

NRSV
"officials of the people"

TEV
"leaders of the nation"

REB
"of high office"

The NKJV has the literal (BDB 978 construct BDB 766). This would imply they are high government leaders.
The problem comes in how to identify them because most of these leaders were exiled with Ezekiel and the royal court
(597 B.C.). These may have been:

- some who escaped capture and deportation and were idolators ‒ Ezek. 8

- some of lesser stature who assumed the role of leadership in the vacuum caused by the exile

In context, option #1 is best because Ezekiel is taken by the Spirit to Jerusalem.

11:2 "Son of man" See note at Ezek. 2:1.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SON OF MAN

▣ "who devise iniquity and give evil advice in the city" Their attitude is depicted in Ezek. 11:3
and 15. They are false leaders (cf. Ezek. 11:4), so common in Israel's religious and civic life!

11:3 "Is it not time to build houses? This city is the pot and we are the flesh" What they were saying is

- "We are the chosen ones. Those who were exiled were judged by God, but He is not going to judge us who
remain in the chosen city! We are His choicest vessels" (cf. Ezek. 28:26; Jer. 29:5, i.e. build
houses in Jerusalem now! Also note Jer. 21:8-10, where the prophets were preaching "Peace, peace"
and yet the destruction of Babylon is surely coming).

- The phrase "to build houses" may be an idiom for starting a family (or family line, cf. Deut. 25:9;
Ruth 4:11).
Not only is the first phrase in doubt, but also the second. It could be

- imagery for protection

- imagery for destruction

All being noted, I think it is a parallel to the false prophets' message of

- peace is sure

- the city will never fall

- we who remain are the chosen ones

- YHWH has already rejected us, why should we serve Him?

- Let us prepare for war (i.e. build fortifications, not build houses)!

The false, idolatrous leaders are the cause of Jerusalem's fall (cf. v. 6). The imagery here
is from a sacrificial offering. The people of Jerusalem are the meat offering and the city is the sacrificial pot
they are cooked in (i.e. siege, cf. v. 7)!

Notice v. 11 negates this prediction of the false, idolatrous leaders. YHWH will judge
them, not in the city but at the borders of Israel.

- as they try to escaape

- as they go into Neo-Babylonian exile

- they were executed at Riblah (cf. 2 Kgs. 25:18-21; Jer. 52:24-27)

11:4 "prophesy against them" Ezekiel had done this earlier in Ezek. 3:4,17.

The verb "prophesy" (BDB 612, KB 659) is a Niphal
imperative. It is used twice for emphasis! YHWH, by His Spirit, directed the
prophet (Ezek. 11:5) what to say, when to say it, and who to say it to.

SPECIAL TOPIC: PROPHECY (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: INSPIRATION

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: EZEKIEL 11:5-12

5Then the Spirit of the Lord fell upon me, and He said to
me, "Say, 'Thus says the Lord, "So you think, house of Israel, for I know your thoughts. 6You have multiplied
your slain in this city, filling its streets with them." 7Therefore, thus says the Lord God, "Your slain whom you
have laid in the midst of the city are the flesh and this city is the pot; but I will bring you out of it. 8You have feared a sword; so I will bring
a sword upon you," the Lord God declares. 9"And I will bring you out of the midst of the city and deliver you
into the hands of strangers and execute judgments against you. 10You will fall by the sword. I will judge you to the border of Israel; so you shall
know that I am the Lord. 11This city will not be a pot for you, nor will you be flesh in the midst of it, but
I will judge you to the border of Israel. 12Thus you will know that I am the Lord; for you have not walked in My statutes
nor have you executed My ordinances, but have acted according to the ordinances of the nations around you."'"

11:5 "said. . .say. . .says" The Hebrew word "say" (BDB 55, KB 65) is found often in this chapter.
It refers to

- YHWH speaking to and through Ezekiel

- the false leaders speaking

- Ezekiel praying to YHWH

See note at Ezek. 11:4. Ezekiel is YHWH's mouthpiece!

▣ "I know your thoughts" This same truth is expressed in several ways (cf. 1 Sam. 16:7; 1 Chr. 28:9;
Ps. 7:9; Prov. 16:2; 21:2; 24:12; Jer. 11:20; 17:10; Luke 16:15; Acts 1:24; 15:8; Rom. 8:27; Rev. 2:23). God
knows the thoughts and motives of His human creatures! We reap what we sow (see full lists of texts at Gal. 6:7-10 online) and what we think!

The literal phrase is "what comes up in your spirit"( NASB margin). The Hebrew term "spirit,"
"wind," "breath" (BDB 924) is understood here as "mind" (cf. Ezek. 20:32).

SPECIAL TOPIC: BREATH, WIND, SPIRIT

11:6 The terrible judgment about to destroy Jerusalem and the temple (God's protected place, Jer. 7:26)
is because of their evil, not a lack of YHWH's power to protect nor His compassion to care!

11:7 This statement reverses the false leaders' statement of confidence in Ezek. 11:3.

11:9 "I shall deliver you into the hands of" This is an idiom of military defeat.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HAND

▣ "of strangers" This is a fulfillment of Deut. 28:36,49,50. As Assyrians exiled the northern tribes,
so Neo-Babylon will exile the southern tribes!

11:10 "so you shall know that I am the Lord" See note at Ezek. 6:13.

▣ "to the borders of Israel" This could be "as far as the borders of Israel," or it could refer
to "at the borders of Israel" as fulfilled in 2 Kings 25:18-21, where King Zedekiah, when trying to fleeing,
is captured and taken to Nebuchadnezzar II at Riblah.

11:11 This is a clarification of Ezek. 11:7.

11:12 Israel sinned against two "laws."

- the statutes and ordinances of YHWH (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: TERMS FOR GOD'S REVELATION; known
as "special revelation," cf. Ps. 19:7-12)

- the society norms of the surrounding nations (cf. Ezek. 5:7; known as "natural revelation," cf. Ps. 19:1-6;
Rom. 1:19; 2:14)

Israel "walked" (i.e. lifestyle actions, BDB 229, KB 246, Qal PERFECT)
in ways more evil than their pagan neighbors. This demanded judgment (cf. Gen. 15:16; Lev. 18:24-30).

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: EZEKIEL 11:13

13Now it came about as I prophesied, that Pelatiah son of Benaiah died. Then I fell on my
face and cried out with a loud voice and said, "Alas, Lord God! Will You bring the remnant of Israel to a complete end?"

11:13 "it came about as I prophesied, that Pelatiah son of Benaiah died" This was a visible and immediate
sign to the elders back in the exile of the validity of Ezekiel's message. The word of this man's death would
not reach them for several weeks.

▣ "Alas, Lord God!" This is literally the divine title "Adon YHWH."

SPECIAL TOPIC: LORD (Adon and Kurios)

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

▣ Will You bring the remnant of Israel to a complete end" This
same question was asked by Ezekiel as the six angelic destroyers went through the city (Ezek. 9:8).

It is uncertain why the death of an evil leader (Ezek. 11:2) would illicit this response.

For the theological concept of "remnant" see
SPECIAL TOPIC: THE REMNANT (three senses).

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: EZEKIEL 11:14-21

14Then the word of the Lord came to me, saying,
15"Son of man, your brothers, your relatives, your fellow exiles and the whole house of Israel, all of them, are those to whom the
inhabitants of Jerusalem have said, 'Go far from the Lord; this land has been given us as a possession.' 16Therefore
say, 'Thus says the Lord God, "Though I had removed them far away among the nations and though I had scattered them
among the countries, yet I was a sanctuary for them a little while in the countries where they had gone."' 17Therefore say, 'Thus says the Lord
God, "I will gather you from the peoples and assemble you out of the countries among which you have been scattered, and I
will give you the land of Israel."' 18When they come there, they will remove all its detestable things and all its abominations from it. 19And
I will give them one heart, and put a new spirit within them. And I will take the heart of stone out of their flesh and give them a heart of flesh, 20that
they may walk in My statutes and keep My ordinances and do them. Then they will be My people, and I shall be their God. 21But as for those whose
hearts go after their detestable things and abominations, I will bring their conduct down on their heads," declares the Lord God.

11:15 "Son of man" See note at Ezek. 2:1.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SON OF MAN

NASB, NRSV
"your fellow exiles"

NASB margin, Jewish Study Bible
"the men of your

redemption"

NKJV, Peshitta
"your kinsmen"

NRSV footnote
"people of your kindred"

NJB, REB
"to your kinfolk"

LXX
"the men of thy captivity"

JPSOA
"the men of your kindred"

The MT has "the men of your kindred" (BDB 35 construct BDB 145), which seems to refer to other
exiles, possibly of the same tribe clan or family.

For "kindred" (i.e. Go'el) see notes at Ruth 3:9.

SPECIAL TOPIC: KINSMAN REDEEMER

▣ "Go far from the Lord; this land has been given us as a possession" "Go
far" (BDB 934, KB 1221) can be a Qal IMPERATIVE or a Qal
PERFECT. This is related to verse 3. The current residents of Jerusalem were
saying they were the new chosen seed and the exiles (the royal family, the civil and religious leaders, and
the artisans) had been rejected. But in reality just the opposite was true. This can be seen in Ezek. 11:16,
where God says, "I am going to dwell with the exiles" and Ezek. 11:17, where He says He will restore them to
the land. Both Ezek. 11:16 and 17 start with an IMPERATIVE!

Although it is true that Ezekiel focuses on Judah's destruction and exile through chapter 24
(chapters 25-32 are oracles against the nations, except for 28:25-26), there are hints here and there in these
early chapters of Ezekiel's message of restoration to the faithful remnant exiled in Mesopotamia.

- Ezek. 5:3

- Ezek. 6:8-9

- Ezek. 11:14-21

- Ezek. 12:16

- Ezek. 16:60-63

- Ezek. 17:22-24

- Ezek. 20:39-44

- Ezek. 28:25-26

11:16 "I was a sanctuary for them" YHWH is described as a place of sacredness and safety to the faithful
exiles (cf. Isa. 8:14, in Isa. 25:4 He is a "refuge"). These are all powerful imagery for care and protection!
The physical sanctuary in Jerusalem will be destroyed, but the "true" sanctuary (i.e. YHWH) was with them in
exile as the visions of Ezekiel would clearly reveal. YHWH had left Jerusalem and moved east (cf. Ezek. 11:22-25),
but He would return with the exiles. YHWH moving to Babylon showed His universality. He was not limited to Canaan.
He was the God of all creation!

This phrase may have been the OT background for Jesus' statement in John 2:19, quoted in Mark 14:58;
15:29; and Acts 6:14. Jesus saw Himself as the new temple! He is our sanctuary!

The term "little" (BDB 589), depending on context, can mean "a little" or "a few." It can denote
numbers, kinds, or time. In this context "time" (i.e. the exile) fits best (NET). YHWH Himself cannot be described
as "a little sanctuary"!

SPECIAL TOPIC: REFUGE

11:17 "the land of Israel" See note at Ezek. 7:2.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ISRAEL (the name)

11:18-19 Notice that "they will remove" (BDB 693, KB 747, Hiphil, PERFECT
with waw, PLURAL) follows Ezek. 18:31-32. However, this has been the problem
of fallen humanity, they cannot keep God's covenant! Therefore, YHWH will act on their behalf (i.e. similar to the "new
covenant" of Jer. 31:31-34; described in Ezek. 36:22-36).

- "I will give," Ezek. 11:19, BDB 678, KB 773, Qal PERFECT with
waw, SINGULAR

- "I shall put, Ezek. 11:19, BDB 678, KB 773, Qal IMPERFECT SINGULAR

The returning exiles were meant to remove all the idolatrous evil from the land. By reading Ezra
and Nehemiah this hope was only partially fulfilled. Idolatry was forsaken, but other evils returned.

11:19 "I shall give them one heart, and shall put a new spirit within them" The MT has "one" heart,
but note the following translations.

- LXX ‒ "another heart"

- Peshitta ‒ "a new heart"

- REB ‒ "singleness of heart"

- NIV ‒ "an undivided heart"

If "one," then it denotes

- loyalty to YHWH

- unity of Jacob's children (cf. Ezek. 37:15-23)

Because of (1) the parallelism within Ezek. 11:19 and (2) the textual parallel of Ezek. 36:26-27,
I think the concept of "new" fits best. Not just restoration, but reorientation from an outward performance
standard to an inner motivation based on divine performance (cf. Deut. 30:3-9). It is not just a new day
for the children of Jacob, but for the children of Adam!

This is the new covenant (cf. Luke 22:20; 1 Cor. 11:25; 2 Cor. 3:3,6; Heb. 8:6-13; 9:15; 12:24)
described in Jer. 31:31-34 and Ezek. 36:22-36. Israel had been characterized by Moses as being stiff-necked,
hard-faced, and hard-hearted (see SPECIAL TOPIC: STUBBORNNESS);
now they will have a soft heart (i.e. obedient heart, cf. Ezek. 36:27) that is turned toward God (cf. Ezek. 16:60-63).

This is a good example of both God's sovereignty and individual responsibility in the sense that
this same phrase is repeated in Ezek. 18:31, where the people are commanded to make themselves a new heart
and a new spsirit. Yet, again in Ezek. 36:26, it says that YHWH will give them a new heart and a new spirit. Here
is the paradox of God's sovereignty and human responsibility! At this point let me insert three theological
Special Topics that deal with this issue.

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- Why did the elders come to Ezekiel?

- What does the series of idolatry in chapter 8 mean?

- Why is the description of the Cherubim and the portable throne chariot in chapter 10 slightly different from chapter 1?

- Why is Ezek. 11:16 and 23 so significant to the exiles?

- Describe the significance of Ezek. 11:19 in relationship to the New Covenant of Jeremiah and the NT emphasis on individual responsibility.
